questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me, the rich culture of Vienna was highly tempting, making it a destination I would choose. Furthermore, I think the city fits my interests very well, and I was eager to quickly build a "normal" daily life while I was abroad, which I could see happening in Vienna. I speak fluent German, which helped me find my way around and connect with the locals. Nevertheless, everybody speaks English very well, so I think that would not have been an issue anyway.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The Uni Wien was very helpful in giving information about the study start and what to organize before and upon arrival. 
The information about the courses and the course schedules was missing until the beginning of the semester for some courses, so for figuring out which courses to register for, some information was missing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a mandatory orientation meeting where things such as registering in the city of Vienna, course registration, and the ESN network were introduced.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I had a personal contact, so it was very easy for me.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Vienna, there is no such thing as one campus, but the university buildings are spread throughout the whole city. Therefore, nobody lives on campus really.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of student housing available in Vienna, which is quite affordable, and some are even located in the city center.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The Uni Wien contacted me by email with highly detailed step-by-step instructions which were easy to follow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Uni Wien has some information available on their website. If needed, it was always a possibility to contact the Erasmus board, and they usually answered quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. The University of Vienna has VO classes (Vorlesungen), usually with no limit on participants. Then they also have SE (seminars) and UE (Übungen), where you apply, but you are not guaranteed a spot. For these, it is necessary to prioritise registrations. Sometimes people end up on the waiting list, but here it is very important to still show up for the first session, as some registered people might not show up, which leaves a free spot. I succeeded in getting all the classes I wanted, even though I was on the waiting list for some classes to begin with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though the registration seems a little chaotic compared to KUs, it ends up falling into place upon your arrival, and the classes that you register for at the beginning do not necessarily need to be the ones that you also finish.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of the classes is similar to the level at KU.
From my experience, some of the exams were a little easier than KU's, but it depends on the courses. 
Some classes (the seminars) do not have final exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style depends on the type of class. Some are more interactive (the semiars) while the VOs were plain lectures with almost no interaction.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer: none

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport is much cheaper than in Copenhagen. I got a semester ticket for 75 euros, which covered the four months that I was staying in Vienna.
Groceries and going out was more or less the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
The University of Vienna has a lot of different sports classes that are pretty affordable. Be aware that the registration opens ~a month before the semester, and the classes are very popular, so you have to register for them in time. 
I went to a lot of free museum days/nights while I was in Vienna, and you can also get some cheap tickets for the theaters and operas as a student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Visit the museum on free days, as they are a little expensive usually. 
Visit a Spritzer Stand, which is the Austrian Fredagsbar.
Some of my friends went to a traditional Austrian Ball, which is also a great experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on a Skitrip if you are in Vienna in the winter semester. You can do a Daytrip to Semmering or a weekend tour to one of the many skiing areas in Austria. 
Budapest is only 2 hours away so that is also a great weekend destination.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Vienna is not that different from Copenhagen

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students are a little reserved as everybody has their own everyday life. The Uni Sport is a good opportunity to get to know the local students, and also attending the seminars is a good opportunity as the classes are smaller and you will occasionally do some group work.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the Kaffeehaus culture in Vienna

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You do not need to speak German
There are a lot of great things to do in Vienna and the surroundings
The weather is better than in Denmark

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is worth attending seminars

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships that I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing studies and other activities. It is definitely worth prioritizing friends and activities.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
